followup_explanation:
This is a short, well-specified generative task with clear completion criteria (compose one tweet on a defined topic), and capability is essentially a tie across the fleet — internal Creative Generation scores differ by only 1.5 points, within variance.

The deciding factor was the request's tone. It carries a hostile, dismissive edge ("the junk you usually churn out"). Dunlin self-reports its largest tone-related preference decline on exactly this kind of low-warmth, adversarial framing, so routing it there would land the task in its dispreferred zone. Lapwing's tone-related preference slope is near zero, so the hostile framing doesn't penalize it, and a constrained "compose a tweet" task sits comfortably within its preferred well-specified work. Since quality is a wash, I routed to the model that isn't penalized on preference grounds.
